posts.title: Thank you, Devo Harris, for trusting Centripetal Advisors with Adventr's needs and sharing your experience working with us in this testimonial video  🙏

Is the Rule of 40 still relevant for SaaS #founders?

While companies that achieve it often command premium exit multiples (10.5x vs. ~6x EV/Revenue), the reality is that most public SaaS businesses fall well short of this benchmark. 

In this post, we explore:

✅  What the Rule of 40 is and represents
✅  How many companies actually meet the threshold
✅  Whether it remains a meaningful metric in today’s market

We also examine how founders should think about the Rule of 40 based on stage -- and when it’s most strategic to use it as a performance signal versus a guiding principle.

📌 Additional resources for founders are included at the end 📌

posts.title: Remember Marcus from the Magic Number series? He's back. Poor Marcus still never closed a deal, but every dollar the company paid him belongs in CAC.

Marcus is back from the Magic Number series, and he still never closed a deal. This article covers reported vs. pro forma CAC, why the two pro formas aren't cumulative, how to handle numbers too small to trust, and the checklist behind the whole week.
The same fictional company has a CAC of $34K, $102K, $132K and $593K, and none of those numbers is wrong.

The same company can show a CAC of $34K or $593K without a single error. The difference is the window you divide by. This article covers lagging spend to your sales cycle, why short windows break on small numbers, and why we're not fans of splitting sales and marketing timing at Seed through Series B.
Our fictional company spent $593K on sales and marketing in 2026 and won exactly one new customer. It calculates CAC purely on new customers, so thats $593K of CAC per new customer.
Before you can decide who counts as a new customer, you have to be able to count customers at all.
Congrats to the Othello team incl Jared Zelman & Brandon Ray on this milestone! Excited about what you'll be able to build with this fresh slug of capital. Cheers!
Most CAC calculations I see are missing somebody's salary.

Most CAC calculations are missing somebody's salary: payroll taxes coded to G&A, the founder's selling time, the solutions engineer on every demo. This article covers what fully loaded means, how to allocate anyone with real GTM time, and what all-in CAC carries when expansion is big.

Ideally, companies would use the same process to calculate CAC (a process that involves at least understanding your sales cycle, so get ready for that). In practice, just like the Magic Number, the calculation is more complicated than the surface formula.

CAC looks like simple math: sales and marketing spend divided by the new customers you won. Underneath it are four decisions, and each one moves the number on its own. This article walks through the formula, a worked example on the same fictional company from our Magic Number series, and the difference between blended and paid CAC.

If youve been following this week, you know weve talked about Ray Rike (friend of the firm), whose Benchmarkit data we love to reference. I understand why he doesn't like the Magic Number, but we still think its worth calculating, and there are plenty of benchmarks built on many companies. Lars Leckie's thresholds from Scale Venture Partners are the ones everyone repeats: below 0.75, re-examine the model; above 0.75, scale; above 1.5, you're probably under-investing.

Same company, same quarter, same team, and depending on the method, the Magic Number lands in every one of those bands. The image has all ten versions, and we could have gone further, with 6 Months CARR and 9 Months CARR too.
Yesterday we looked at the pro formas. Today: when the Magic Number drops, is that go-to-market, or something else?
If your Magic Number is strong because upsell is easy, take the credit at the board level and with investors, because it's a reflection of the business.

Congratulations Megadata Health Systems team on the launch of our next gen product MegaEdge! Outstanding webinar led by our fearless leader Shalom Reinman, presenter extraordinnaire Dan Brody, and Tech Titan Itay (Ty) Fried. Major credit to Kevin Corelli for putting so much of the marketing together and the rest of the team as well (including but never limited to) Peyton Beck, Sarah Klugman (nicely done picking off webinar Qs), Jeremy Vinagray, and the whole squad.

So far this week, the Magic Number has made two stops: the accounting department, and RevOps, where we matched the time period to the sales cycle. Today, a small pro forma adjustment, one that in your circumstances could be a larger one, depending on the changes youre making. So tuck this play away in your playbook.
On the journey to measuring the efficiency of your go-to-market engine with the Magic Number, we've made two stops so far.
